title: iBooks on the iPad, 2010
lede: Apple’s e-book app for the first iPad: a wooden bookshelf for the library and a bound book with stacked page edges for reading.
summary: A bookshelf library and a two-page book spread with page edges and a curling page turn. Apple, 2010.

evidence.note: Inspected a 1280 px copy of [File:1st-Gen-iPad-WiFi-iBooks.jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:1st-Gen-iPad-WiFi-iBooks.jpg) (Evan-Amos, 2011, public-domain photograph of a first-generation iPad showing the iBooks reading view). The photo shows the reading view only. The bookshelf view is documented, not observed. Not stored.

styles.note: The reading view imitates a bound book, and the library imitates a wooden bookshelf: a clear object metaphor from the core years of the style.

context: Apple announced iBooks with the iPad on 27 January 2010. In Book layout, “pages are turned by tapping or dragging the page, animated to imitate the appearance of a paper book.” [Wikipedia: Apple Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Books).
NN/g: “Ereaders, like iBooks and Kindle, were designed to look like physical bookshelves.” [NN/g: Skeuomorphism](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/skeuomorphism/).

On the day of the announcement, TechCrunch wrote that “the bookshelf view in iBooks is nearly identical to the main bookshelf view used in Delicious Library”; Wil Shipley noted that Mike Matas, a former Delicious Monster designer, worked on the iPad interface. [TechCrunch, MG Siegler, 27 January 2010](https://techcrunch.com/2010/01/27/think-ibooks-looks-familiar-youre-not-the-only-one/). See [Delicious Library](ref:delicious-library-2004).
observed: In landscape the screen shows two facing pages with a dark shadow in the gutter.
Thin stacked page edges run down the outer sides of both pages, as on a thick closed book block.
The pages are off-white; text is set in a serif face, justified and hyphenated.
A small bar at the top holds “Library” and table-of-contents buttons with a light bevel.
interpretation: The reading view carries non-functional detail from the physical book (page edges, gutter shadow) while the controls stay small and plain. It is a quieter case than the leather and felt apps.
borrow: Suggest a long document with stacked edge lines at the sides instead of a scroll bar.
Put a soft vertical shadow in the gutter of a two-column reading layout.

rights.statement: Apple software; copyrighted. No image is stored here.
